questions.prompt: What changes as the shokunin acquires new techniques and perspectives?
questions.promptZh: 随着shokunin获得新技法与视角，什么随之变化？
options: The work of the craftsperson.
Only the professional title, while techniques remain unchanged.
The point at which the original devotion must necessarily end.
Only the physical location of the restaurant, rather than its work.
optionsZh: 手艺人的工作。
只有职业头衔，技法保持不变。
最初投入必然终止的时间点。
只有餐厅物理地点，而非工作本身。
analyses: A It回指The work of a shokunin，变化与获得新技法、视角相连。
B 原句说new techniques，不能改为技法始终固定、只变头衔。
C changes over time并不表示投入必然在某点终止。
D 当前句论工作随学习改变，没有only location的限制。

vocabulary.meaning: 视角；看待事物的方式
vocabulary.context: 此处与新技法一起拓展长期工作，不是餐厅物理座位朝向。
vocabulary.example: New techniques and perspectives can change a craftsperson's work.

questions.evidenceQuote: The work of a shokunin, like Jiro, is different from that of an amateur because it requires lifetime devotion. It changes over time as a shokunin acquires new techniques and perspectives. Jiro somehow finds a way to feel the continuous rejuvenation of his first love for sushi. One way to reach psychological richness is to follow Jiro’s path: devotion to one career, provided that the chosen career is deep enough for lifelong exploration.

questions.prompt: What does Jiro's 'first love' refer to in this passage?
questions.promptZh: 本段中Jiro的first love指什么？
options: A named spouse whose biography is being reported.
His first customer, whom he never saw again.
An entirely new occupation replacing sushi.
His original love for sushi, which he finds ways to renew.
optionsZh: 文中正在介绍生平的一位有姓名配偶。
他从此再没见过的第一位顾客。
替代寿司的全新职业。
他最初对寿司的热爱，并设法让它更新。
analyses: A first love for sushi给清楚对象，不能因前节婚姻话题移为配偶。
B 本句没有第一位顾客叙述。
C 对象仍为sushi，非换业。
D of his first love for sushi与continuous rejuvenation把最初心爱事业和持续活力相连。

vocabulary.meaning: 最初的热爱；最钟爱的早期兴趣
vocabulary.context: 此处带for sushi，指对职业技艺的初衷，不必指某段人际初恋。
vocabulary.example: He continues to renew his first love for the craft.

questions.evidenceQuote: The work of a shokunin, like Jiro, is different from that of an amateur because it requires lifetime devotion. It changes over time as a shokunin acquires new techniques and perspectives. Jiro somehow finds a way to feel the continuous rejuvenation of his first love for sushi. One way to reach psychological richness is to follow Jiro’s path: devotion to one career, provided that the chosen career is deep enough for lifelong exploration.

questions.prompt: What explanatory problem does the opening question introduce?
questions.promptZh: 开头问句引入哪个需要解释的问题？
options: Why neither band ever gained worldwide popularity.
Why the Beatles are much more popular than the Beach Boys in the comparison presented.
Why both groups must have exactly the same number of listeners.
Why the Beach Boys are said to have more monthly listeners than the Beatles.
optionsZh: 为何两乐队从未全球受欢迎。
在所给比较中，为何Beatles比Beach Boys受欢迎得多。
为何两组必定听众数完全相同。
为何说Beach Boys月听众多于Beatles。
analyses: A 末句说both extremely popular worldwide，不能反转。
B Why...so much more popular提出差异的原因问题；后面听众数字提供写作时背景。
C so much more和数字差异均非相同。
D 比较方向颠倒；数字由as of this writing限定，非实时平台查询。

vocabulary.meaning: 截至作者写作时
vocabulary.context: 把Spotify听众数据锚定原书写作时间，不是网站每次打开时实时更新的统计。
vocabulary.example: The figures describe monthly listeners as of this writing.

questions.evidenceQuote: Why are the Beatles so much more popular than the Beach Boys? Looking at Spotify, the Beach Boys have an astonishing 11,861,427 monthly listeners, as of this writing. However, the Beatles have a mind-blowing 30,561,926 monthly listeners, almost three times that of the Beach Boys. They were both extremely popular worldwide in the 1960s.

questions.prompt: What shared historical feature does the final sentence identify?
questions.promptZh: 末句指出两乐队共有的哪项历史特点？
options: Both had the same number of listeners during every year of their careers.
Only one of the bands was popular beyond its home country.
Both were extremely popular worldwide during the 1960s.
Both first became popular only at the later moment of the Spotify comparison.
optionsZh: 两者生涯每年听众数相同。
只有一个乐队在本国以外受欢迎。
两者在1960年代都极受全球欢迎。
两者直到后来Spotify比较时才首次受欢迎。
analyses: A both popular不等于每年数量相同，没有连续年数据。
B both与worldwide一起肯定两者，非仅一个。
C both、extremely popular、worldwide、1960s逐项对应。
D were...in the1960s给过去背景，不能把写作时数字当首次成名时间。

vocabulary.meaning: 在全世界范围；全球地
vocabulary.context: 在此修饰受欢迎的范围，不能缩成一间大学，也不等于人人都喜欢。
vocabulary.example: Both bands were widely popular worldwide in the period described.

questions.evidenceQuote: Why are the Beatles so much more popular than the Beach Boys? Looking at Spotify, the Beach Boys have an astonishing 11,861,427 monthly listeners, as of this writing. However, the Beatles have a mind-blowing 30,561,926 monthly listeners, almost three times that of the Beach Boys. They were both extremely popular worldwide in the 1960s.

questions.prompt: What is the final 'Why' asking the author to account for?
questions.promptZh: 末尾Why要求解释什么？
options: The observed college-listening difference despite similar active periods and comparable album counts.
The exact date when the two bands first met one another.
The absence of any album releases from either band.
The fact that students had been randomly assigned to listen to different bands.
optionsZh: 活跃期相近、专辑数相当，却出现作者所见大学生听众差异。
两乐队首次见面的精确日期。
两乐队都从未发行专辑。
学生被随机分组听不同乐队这一事实。
analyses: A Yet标出相似条件与观察差异的张力，Why接着寻求解释。
B 段落没有相见日期的话题。
C comparable numbers of albums表示都有专辑，非全无发行。
D I see是作者观察，没有随机听歌实验。

vocabulary.meaning: 可比较、相近的；大致相当的
vocabulary.context: 此处修饰专辑数量，未声称每张专辑内容相同或总数精确相等。
vocabulary.example: The bands released comparable numbers of albums.

questions.evidenceQuote: The two bands were active for similar periods and released comparable numbers of albums. Yet today I see more college students listening to the Beatles than the Beach Boys. Why?

questions.prompt: How does the passage explain a source of the Beatles' variety?
questions.promptZh: 本段怎样解释Beatles多样性的一项来源？
options: It reports four composing members contributing exactly equal song totals.
It attributes the greater variety only to a longer period of activity.
It treats Brian Wilson as one of the three composing Beatles members.
It contrasts three composing Beatles members with Brian Wilson as the Beach Boys' solo composer.
optionsZh: 说四名作曲成员贡献完全相同歌曲数。
把更大多样性仅归于活跃更久。
把Brian Wilson认作三名Beatles作曲成员之一。
以Beatles三名作曲成员对比本段所说Beach Boys的单独作曲者Brian Wilson。
analyses: A 本句three且没有各自完全相同曲数。
B 此处联系创作成员与多样性，未把更久活跃当唯一原因。
C Wilson属本句Beach Boys一侧，不能移入John、Paul、George三人。
D giving them more variety给作者提出的联系；按原段表述作答，不把它扩为完整音乐史名录。

vocabulary.meaning: 作曲；创作歌曲
vocabulary.context: 此处members composing songs限定成员的创作角色，不仅是现场演唱。
vocabulary.example: The account highlights three members composing songs.

questions.evidenceQuote: They had three members composing songs, John, Paul, and George, giving them more variety than the Beach Boys, with Brian Wilson as a solo composer. Wilson is famously innovative and experimental, so the Beach Boys did produce diverse songs. But for a casual music lover, the Beach Boys are often equated with “Surfin’ U.S.A.”: “Everybody’s gone surfin’, surfin’ U.S.A.” If the Beach Boys’ Pet Sounds had been played more often than Surfin’ U.S.A., more people might have been interested in the Beach Boys.

questions.prompt: Why does the author stress that Wilson was innovative and experimental?
questions.promptZh: 作者为何强调Wilson创新而富于实验性？
options: To deny that the Beach Boys ever produced any musical variety.
To acknowledge that the Beach Boys also made diverse songs, despite the preceding contrast.
To prove every casual listener knew the full range of their work.
To state that no listener associated them with a particular song.
optionsZh: 否认Beach Boys曾有任何多样性。
在前面对比之后承认Beach Boys也创作了多样歌曲。
证明每位普通听众都了解他们全部作品。
说无人把他们与某一首歌相联系。
analyses: A so...did produce diverse songs明确为肯定，did加强强调。
B 这句对前一比较加限定：一名作曲者不等于从无多样作品。
C 后面casual music lover可能只联想某歌，不能推每人都了解全部。
D 后文often equated with某歌与无人联想相反。

vocabulary.meaning: 确实创作了；did用于强调肯定
vocabulary.context: 这里不是过去否定式，也不是把创新全部让给Beatles；它承认Beach Boys的实际多样性。
vocabulary.example: The author emphasises that the band did produce diverse songs.

questions.evidenceQuote: They had three members composing songs, John, Paul, and George, giving them more variety than the Beach Boys, with Brian Wilson as a solo composer. Wilson is famously innovative and experimental, so the Beach Boys did produce diverse songs. But for a casual music lover, the Beach Boys are often equated with “Surfin’ U.S.A.”: “Everybody’s gone surfin’, surfin’ U.S.A.” If the Beach Boys’ Pet Sounds had been played more often than Surfin’ U.S.A., more people might have been interested in the Beach Boys.

questions.prompt: What does the question about eating out and hanging out express?
questions.promptZh: 关于外食与相聚的问句表达什么？
options: A confirmed timetable for the end of all restrictions.
An invitation from the narrator to the website user today.
The narrator's uncertainty about resuming ordinary social activities during the 2020 confinement.
A claim that the narrator had already resumed travelling to Japan.
optionsZh: 所有限制结束的确定时间表。
叙述者今天给网站用户的邀请。
2020年居家期间，叙述者对何时恢复日常社交的不确定。
声称叙述者已恢复回日本旅行。
analyses: A When would提问未知时间，没有给确定日期。
B 是书中2020年经历的叙述，非面向当前用户的邀请。
C eat out/hang out具体化此前stuckness与隔离时的盼望和未知。
D 下一问也问何时能回去，不能读成已完成旅行。

vocabulary.meaning: 与人相聚、闲待；轻松共处
vocabulary.context: 此处为日常社交活动，不是把衣物悬挂在户外。
vocabulary.example: He wondered when he would be able to hang out with friends again.

questions.evidenceQuote: In the summer of 2020, when it was increasingly clear that the pandemic was here to stay, I felt as though there was no way out, a sense of stuckness, and I stayed shut inside all day. When would we be able to eat out and hang out? When could I go back to Japan and see my aging parents? Being locked down at home, we watched a lot of movies.

questions.prompt: What did the household do while locked down at home?
questions.promptZh: 封闭在家时，这家人做了什么？
options: They watched films only after returning from a completed trip to Japan.
They arranged most of their viewing at public cinemas outside the home.
They gave up movies because confinement prevented any shared leisure.
They watched many movies while confined at home.
optionsZh: 完成回日本旅行后才看电影。
大部分在家外公共电影院观影。
因封闭无法共同休闲，所以放弃电影。
封闭在家时看了许多电影。
analyses: A 何时能回日本仍是问题，没有先完成旅行再看电影的条件。
B at home明确地点，不是公共影院。
C watched a lot与放弃相反。
D Being locked down...we watched a lot of movies给背景与行为，未调查所有家庭。

vocabulary.meaning: 处于封闭限制、居家隔离状态
vocabulary.context: 此处描述2020年疫情背景中的生活，不是实时发布的地区政策。
vocabulary.example: Being locked down at home, the family watched films together.

questions.evidenceQuote: In the summer of 2020, when it was increasingly clear that the pandemic was here to stay, I felt as though there was no way out, a sense of stuckness, and I stayed shut inside all day. When would we be able to eat out and hang out? When could I go back to Japan and see my aging parents? Being locked down at home, we watched a lot of movies.

questions.prompt: How is Yesterday introduced in this passage?
questions.promptZh: 本段怎样介绍《Yesterday》？
options: As one of the movies watched, identified as a 2019 film.
As the title of the chef's 2011 documentary.
As a live concert the author attended during lockdown.
As a 1960s documentary proving that nobody remembered the Beatles.
optionsZh: 作为看过的电影之一，并标为2019年影片。
作为厨师2011年纪录片的片名。
作为作者封闭期间现场参加的演唱会。
作为证明无人记得Beatles的1960年代纪录片。
analyses: A One of them...2019 movie明确给对象类别与年份。
B 2011厨师纪录片是此前Jiro一节，不是这里。
C movie不是作者现场演唱会。
D 主人公独记Beatles是虚构情节，非1960年代纪录片作出的现实证明。

vocabulary.meaning: 其中之一；属于前面已提的集合
vocabulary.context: 此处回指所看电影集合，而非歌曲、厨师或研究组。
vocabulary.example: One of them was a film released in 2019.

questions.evidenceQuote: One of them was the 2019 movie Yesterday. The protagonist, a struggling singer, realizes that he is the only person who remembers the Beatles and starts singing the Beatles’ songs and becomes famous. The movie was OK. Still, it was memorable for a completely different reason other than the plot.

questions.prompt: What happens to the protagonist in the film's plot as summarised here?
questions.promptZh: 按此处梗概，电影主角经历什么？
options: He interviews Jiro about the best way to prepare sushi.
He remembers the Beatles when others do not and becomes famous by singing their songs.
He proves by experiment that the Beatles never existed in real history.
He writes every Beatles song before discovering that everyone already remembers them.
optionsZh: 采访Jiro怎样做寿司。
在别人不记得时仍记得Beatles，并靠唱他们的歌成名。
以实验证明现实历史从无Beatles。
先写了全部Beatles歌曲，再发现人人都记得。
analyses: A 别部纪录片主题被误移到这里。
B only person who remembers、starts singing、becomes famous给梗概中的次序。
C 这是小说电影情节，不是现实历史实验。
D remembers与sings不是说他原创，only person也非人人都记得。

vocabulary.meaning: 主角；故事中的中心人物
vocabulary.context: 这里是电影中的艰难谋生歌手，不能把其虚构处境当作作者现实经历。
vocabulary.example: The protagonist becomes known for singing songs he remembers.

questions.evidenceQuote: One of them was the 2019 movie Yesterday. The protagonist, a struggling singer, realizes that he is the only person who remembers the Beatles and starts singing the Beatles’ songs and becomes famous. The movie was OK. Still, it was memorable for a completely different reason other than the plot.

questions.prompt: What prompted the narrator's tears while watching the film?
questions.promptZh: 看电影时，什么引出了叙述者的眼泪？
options: The film's plot alone, independently of any song.
His children's tears, which the passage says began before his own.
The main character's singing of The Long and Winding Road.
His own live performance of the song in front of his family.
optionsZh: 只有情节，与歌曲无关。
孩子先哭，随后带动他哭。
主角演唱《The Long and Winding Road》。
他本人在家人面前现场唱歌。
analyses: A 后句lyrics captured how I felt联系歌曲，不能改成情节独立起因。
B 只明确I could not stop crying，没有孩子先哭的记录。
C When连接主角演唱与作者哭，后句解释歌词贴合自身感受。
D 演唱者是main character，作者是观众，角色不可交换。

vocabulary.meaning: 止不住哭；情绪反应难以抑制
vocabulary.context: 在此为叙述者描述自己的观影反应，不说明每个人都会有同样体验。
vocabulary.example: He could not stop crying when the song captured his feelings.

questions.evidenceQuote: When the main character sings “The Long and Winding Road,” I just could not stop crying. I was watching it with my wife and two teenage kids, so it was very embarrassing. But its lyrics captured how I felt during COVID.

questions.prompt: Why was the narrator embarrassed by his reaction?
questions.promptZh: 叙述者为何对自己的反应感到尴尬？
options: He was crying while watching with his wife and two teenage children.
He regarded the plot as poor and regretted choosing it for the family.
His family had asked him to stop singing the song aloud.
He could not recall a song title that his children already knew.
optionsZh: 他与妻子及两个青少年孩子一起看时哭了。
他嫌情节差，后悔为家人选片。
家人要求他不要大声唱那首歌。
他记不起孩子们已经知道的歌名。
analyses: A I was watching...with my wife and two teenage kids，so把家人面前的哭泣与尴尬相连。
B 本段尴尬直接接哭泣与家人在场，未说因选片后悔。
C 是角色唱、作者哭，不能把演唱主体换成作者。
D 没有孩子认出而作者忘记歌名的叙述。

vocabulary.meaning: 令人尴尬的；使人不自在的
vocabulary.context: 此处是作者觉得自己在妻儿面前哭的情境尴尬，不是断定影片质量差。
vocabulary.example: Crying in front of his family felt embarrassing to him.

questions.evidenceQuote: When the main character sings “The Long and Winding Road,” I just could not stop crying. I was watching it with my wife and two teenage kids, so it was very embarrassing. But its lyrics captured how I felt during COVID.

questions.prompt: What reason is given for finding new things in these familiar artists?
questions.promptZh: 为何能在这些熟悉艺术家身上持续发现新东西？
options: Their complete work consists of only one identical song.
They left extensive and varied bodies of work that reward deeper exploration.
The listener must forget every previous encounter before listening again.
Each artist releases a new work every time a listener returns.
optionsZh: 他们全部作品只有一首完全相同的歌。
他们留下丰厚多样的作品，值得深入探索。
听众须先忘掉每次既往接触才能重听。
听众每次回来，艺术家都必发行新作。
analyses: A abundant,diverse与只有一首相反。
B as引出原因，作品的丰厚与多样为深入再发现提供空间。
C 熟悉对象也可新发现，未以遗忘为前提。
D left bodies of work指已留下的作品，不要求每次有实时新发行。

vocabulary.meaning: 作品群；某创作者成体系的作品总量
vocabulary.context: body在此不是身体或尸体，复数bodies对应多位艺术家各自作品。
vocabulary.example: A diverse body of work can reward repeated exploration.

questions.evidenceQuote: With the Beatles, Bob Dylan, and Aretha Franklin, you can go deep and always find something new, as they left abundant, diverse bodies of work. Still, it is important to distinguish between nostalgia and psychological richness. Many people keep listening to the same bands because of nostalgia. Here the main activity is the reenactment of the past, returning to the same familiar comfort zone.

questions.prompt: According to the passage, why do many people keep returning to the same bands?
questions.promptZh: 按本段，许多人为什么不断听同样的乐队？
options: Because repeated listening always means the songs have been newly composed.
Because they have no memory of the music from earlier years.
Because nostalgia draws them back to a familiar past.
Because every return to a familiar band is necessarily a new discovery.
optionsZh: 因为重听总意味着歌曲刚刚被创作。
因为完全不记得早年的音乐。
因为怀旧使他们回到熟悉过去。
因为每次重返熟悉乐队都必定是新发现。
analyses: A 新的聆听与作品刚创作不是同一件事，本句明确给怀旧动机。
B nostalgia关涉过去记忆与眷恋，不是完全没有记忆。
C because of nostalgia直接给原因，后句重演过去加以说明。
D 同一段区分怀旧与新发现，不能说每次重听必有新发现；Many也不是全部听众。

vocabulary.meaning: 怀旧；对自己过去带感伤色彩的向往
vocabulary.context: 这里解释部分重复聆听的动机，不表示每次重听都只有这个原因。
vocabulary.example: Nostalgia can draw a listener back to familiar music.

questions.evidenceQuote: With the Beatles, Bob Dylan, and Aretha Franklin, you can go deep and always find something new, as they left abundant, diverse bodies of work. Still, it is important to distinguish between nostalgia and psychological richness. Many people keep listening to the same bands because of nostalgia. Here the main activity is the reenactment of the past, returning to the same familiar comfort zone.

questions.prompt: Which benefit of nostalgia is explicitly included?
questions.promptZh: 文中明确包括怀旧的哪项益处？
options: A guarantee that every repeated song becomes a new psychological discovery.
A weakening of the connection between past and present.
A permanent guarantee of happiness regardless of later experience.
A sense of connection between one's past and present.
optionsZh: 保证每次重听都有心理新发现。
削弱过去与现在的联系。
不论后来经历怎样都保证永久快乐。
感到个人过去与现在相连。
analyses: A 下句正区分怀旧与心理丰富，未作每次发现的保证。
B connection的正面联系不能改成削弱。
C 列出的益处有限定，未给永久快乐或不受未来事件影响的保证。
D ranging from...connection明确列出，也包含社会联结与意义，并非只此一项。

vocabulary.meaning: 带感伤色彩的向往；情感上的眷恋
vocabulary.context: 破折号中用它解释nostalgia，方向为one’s past，不是计划未来收益。
vocabulary.example: The author defines nostalgia as sentimental longing for one's past.

questions.evidenceQuote: To be clear, nostalgia—sentimental longing for one’s past—has a number of benefits, ranging from a sense of connection between one’s past and present, to social connectedness, to helping us find meaning in our lives. However, listening to the same band for the sake of nostalgia does not increase psychological richness. In contrast, if you keep listening to the same band because you keep noticing something you didn’t notice before, that is a psychologically rich experience, one of finding richness in a familiar object.

questions.prompt: What precise limit does the author place on listening for nostalgia?
questions.promptZh: 作者给为怀旧而聆听设下哪项准确界限？
options: Listening solely for nostalgia is not said to increase psychological richness, although nostalgia has other benefits.
Nostalgia has no benefits of any kind and should never be experienced.
All listening to the same band prevents discovery regardless of the listener's attention.
Psychological richness requires that familiar artists never be heard again.
optionsZh: 单为怀旧听歌并不增加心理丰富，但怀旧仍有其他益处。
怀旧没有任何好处，永远不该体验。
不论怎样注意，所有重听都阻止发现。
心理丰富要求再也不能听熟悉艺术家。
analyses: A for the sake of nostalgia限定动机，前句已承认benefits，不能把某维度的区分变成全盘否定。
B To be clear列出好处，与毫无益处相反。
C 后句明确在重听中注意新东西可心理丰富。
D familiar object可以发现丰富，非必须全部陌生。

vocabulary.meaning: 为了；以某种目的或动机为出发点
vocabulary.context: 此处把怀旧作为聆听动机来限定，不是说同一乐队本身无法再有新发现。
vocabulary.example: Listening for the sake of nostalgia differs from listening to discover details.

questions.evidenceQuote: To be clear, nostalgia—sentimental longing for one’s past—has a number of benefits, ranging from a sense of connection between one’s past and present, to social connectedness, to helping us find meaning in our lives. However, listening to the same band for the sake of nostalgia does not increase psychological richness. In contrast, if you keep listening to the same band because you keep noticing something you didn’t notice before, that is a psychologically rich experience, one of finding richness in a familiar object.

questions.prompt: What connection between Woolf and the Beatles opens the section?
questions.promptZh: 本节开头以什么联系Woolf与Beatles？
options: They created exactly the same kind of artistic work.
Woolf composed every Beatles song before writing novels.
They both have enthusiastic audiences across generations.
Their audiences are restricted to people of one birth year.
optionsZh: 他们创作的艺术种类完全相同。
Woolf先创作了全部Beatles歌曲才写小说。
两者都拥有跨世代的热情受众。
他们受众只限同一个出生年份。
analyses: A like在此只比受欢迎的跨世代现象，非媒介相同。
B 小说家与乐队的作品角色被错误混合。
C Like...fans across generations明确给共同点。
D across generations排除只限一个出生年。

vocabulary.meaning: 跨越多代人；不同世代都有
vocabulary.context: 这里说受众跨世代，并非断言每个世代的每个人都喜欢。
vocabulary.example: The writer has enthusiastic fans across generations.

questions.evidenceQuote: Like the Beatles, Virginia Woolf has enthusiastic fans across generations. The novelist Jenny Offill wrote an essay entitled “A Lifetime of Lessons in Mrs. Dalloway” for The New Yorker. She summarizes why it’s possible to read Mrs. Dalloway many times and discover many new things on each read. When she first read it, she was seventeen or eighteen years old.

questions.prompt: Who wrote the essay about a lifetime of lessons in Mrs. Dalloway?
questions.promptZh: 谁写了关于《Mrs. Dalloway》终身启示的文章？
options: Virginia Woolf, introducing her novel in a New Yorker essay.
Jenny Offill, writing for The New Yorker.
Jenny Offill, writing the original novel rather than an essay about it.
An unnamed critic, writing an essay entitled Jenny Offill's Life.
optionsZh: Virginia Woolf为《The New Yorker》写文介绍自己的小说。
Jenny Offill为《The New Yorker》撰写。
Jenny Offill写原小说，而非评论该书的文章。
匿名评论者写题为《Jenny Offill的人生》的文章。
analyses: A 句子主语是Jenny Offill，不能将被讨论小说作者换成文章作者。
B novelist Jenny Offill、wrote an essay、for The New Yorker逐项对应。
C Offill是写关于重读的文章，非原小说创作者。
D 作者有名、标题也明确，不是匿名传记标题。

vocabulary.meaning: 题为；名为
vocabulary.context: 在这里引出文章标题，不是be entitled to所表示的有权获得。
vocabulary.example: She wrote an essay entitled A Lifetime of Lessons in Mrs. Dalloway.

questions.evidenceQuote: Like the Beatles, Virginia Woolf has enthusiastic fans across generations. The novelist Jenny Offill wrote an essay entitled “A Lifetime of Lessons in Mrs. Dalloway” for The New Yorker. She summarizes why it’s possible to read Mrs. Dalloway many times and discover many new things on each read. When she first read it, she was seventeen or eighteen years old.

questions.prompt: How old was Offill when she first read the novel, according to this account?
questions.promptZh: 按此处叙述，Offill初读小说时多大？
options: Exactly thirty, the age assigned to the veteran character.
Already in the fifty-second year described in her later rereading.
In her thirties, when she first noticed Clarissa.
Seventeen or eighteen, rather than one exact stated age.
optionsZh: 恰30岁，与退伍军人人物年龄相同。
已进入后来重读时说的第52年。
30多岁，即首次注意Clarissa的阶段。
十七或十八岁，未给唯一精确年龄。
analyses: A about thirty描述Septimus，不是Offill初读年龄，且也非exact。
B fifty-second year是后来阶段，不是first read。
C thirties为重读阶段，时间被提前。
D seventeen or eighteen明确保留两个可能，不能自行确定17或18之一。

vocabulary.meaning: 初次阅读；第一次读到
vocabulary.context: 当前过去时read与后面again构成阅读人生阶段的顺序，不是首次发表书评的日期。
vocabulary.example: She first read the novel as a teenager.

questions.evidenceQuote: Like the Beatles, Virginia Woolf has enthusiastic fans across generations. The novelist Jenny Offill wrote an essay entitled “A Lifetime of Lessons in Mrs. Dalloway” for The New Yorker. She summarizes why it’s possible to read Mrs. Dalloway many times and discover many new things on each read. When she first read it, she was seventeen or eighteen years old.

questions.prompt: Who is described as about thirty in the quoted introduction?
questions.promptZh: 引述的介绍中，谁被描写为大约30岁？
options: Septimus Warren Smith, the veteran character who captivated Offill.
Jenny Offill at the time of her first teenage reading.
Virginia Woolf when she wrote the essay for The New Yorker.
Peter Walsh in the later account of his fifty-second year.
optionsZh: 吸引Offill的退伍军人人物Septimus Warren Smith。
十几岁初读时的Jenny Offill。
为《The New Yorker》写该文时的Virginia Woolf。
后来处于生命第52年叙述里的Peter Walsh。
analyses: A 前句介绍Septimus，Woolf introduced him的him接此人物；about保留大约。
B Offill初读17或18，不能把人物年龄移给读者。
C 此处Woolf引入小说人物，文章作者在前段是Offill。
D 当前段落对象是Septimus，不是后段Peter。引语是文学描写，不是参与者测量。

vocabulary.meaning: 落下；向下落
vocabulary.context: 在world raised its whip的文学意象中问鞭子将落何处，非研究记录的一次实际鞭打。
vocabulary.example: The image asks where the raised whip will descend.

questions.evidenceQuote: She was captivated by Septimus Warren Smith, the war veteran with a deep trauma. Woolf introduced him as “aged about thirty, pale-faced, beak-nosed,” adding, “The world has raised its whip; where will it descend?” Offill thought, “Yes, this. Exactly this.”

questions.prompt: Whose inner response is introduced by 'thought' in the passage?
questions.promptZh: 段落里thought引出谁的内心反应？
options: Septimus's measured answer to a research questionnaire.
Woolf's reply to an interview with the narrator.
Offill's response as a reader to the character and quoted description.
Clarissa's spoken instruction to Peter at the party.
optionsZh: Septimus在研究问卷中的实测回答。
Woolf在作者访谈中的回复。
读者Offill对人物与所引描写的反应。
Clarissa在聚会上对Peter的口头指令。
analyses: A 不是问卷研究，Septimus是文学人物。
B Offill thought直接标明归属，不是Woolf访谈。
C 叙述从Woolf描写转到Offill读者的心声，Yes,this是该反应的开头。
D Clarissa与Peter属于后面的阅读关注，本处thought也不是spoken instruction。

vocabulary.meaning: 心想；内心作出反应
vocabulary.context: 这里引出Offill阅读时的心声，与前一层Woolf的小说描写区分。
vocabulary.example: Offill thought that the description captured something she recognised.

questions.evidenceQuote: She was captivated by Septimus Warren Smith, the war veteran with a deep trauma. Woolf introduced him as “aged about thirty, pale-faced, beak-nosed,” adding, “The world has raised its whip; where will it descend?” Offill thought, “Yes, this. Exactly this.”

questions.prompt: What does 'Exactly this' do after 'Yes, this'?
questions.promptZh: Yes,this之后的Exactly this起什么作用？
options: It retracts the agreement and says the description is wholly irrelevant.
It intensifies the reader's recognition of the description just quoted.
It gives a precise numerical measure of the veteran's trauma.
It introduces a different speaker without any connection to Offill.
optionsZh: 撤回赞同，说描写完全无关。
加强读者对刚引描写的认同。
给退伍军人创伤的精确数字测量。
引入与Offill毫无关联的另一说话者。
analyses: A Exactly强化前面的Yes，而不是转成No。
B 两个短语共同属于Offill thought的引语，后者强调正是如此的认同。
C exactly在此是强调吻合，不是量表数字或诊断程度。
D 闭引号结束同一内心反应，未切换人物；候选句被分开不代表换人说话。

vocabulary.meaning: 正是；恰恰如此
vocabulary.context: 此处强调与所读描写的共鸣，不提供精确年龄、测量值或新的独立论据。
vocabulary.example: Exactly this reinforces the preceding expression of recognition.

questions.evidenceQuote: She was captivated by Septimus Warren Smith, the war veteran with a deep trauma. Woolf introduced him as “aged about thirty, pale-faced, beak-nosed,” adding, “The world has raised its whip; where will it descend?” Offill thought, “Yes, this. Exactly this.”

questions.prompt: What sequence is marked by the sentence beginning with 'Then'?
questions.promptZh: Then开头的句子标出什么顺序？
options: Woolf wrote the novel only after Offill turned thirty.
The first reading occurred after the final rereading in her fifties.
Offill read a different book with the same title on the same day.
Offill returned to the novel in her thirties, after the earlier teenage reading.
optionsZh: Offill满30岁后Woolf才写小说。
初读发生在五十多岁最后重读之后。
Offill当天读了另一本同名书。
Offill在初读的青少年阶段之后，于30多岁重读。
analyses: A she read it again讲读者重读，非作者写书时间。
B Then在后接Finally之前，不能倒置人生顺序。
C again和同一it保持作品对象，未换书。
D in her thirties与read it again给第二阶段；不把thirties缩为恰30生日。

vocabulary.meaning: 在她30多岁时；30至39岁这一人生阶段
vocabulary.context: 不是恰好30岁，更不是第三次阅读次数本身。
vocabulary.example: She reread the novel in her thirties and noticed a different character.

questions.evidenceQuote: Then, in her thirties, she read it again. This time she was intrigued by Clarissa Dalloway, who noticed things like “the laughing girls taking their absurd woolly dogs for a run.” Finally, Offill read it again as she became Mrs. Dalloway’s age, “just broken into her fifty-second year.” This time, she was moved by Peter Walsh, Clarissa’s old flame, who finds relief in self-distancing; everything becomes less personal.

questions.prompt: How is Offill's final rereading placed in relation to Mrs. Dalloway's age?
questions.promptZh: Offill最后一次重读怎样与Mrs.Dalloway年龄对应？
options: She had reached the character's life stage, described as having just entered her fifty-second year.
She was still seventeen or eighteen, exactly as at the first reading.
She had just completed fifty-two full years, which the quotation explicitly states.
She was in her thirties, the only age at which she read the book.
optionsZh: 到了人物同样的人生阶段，引语说刚进入生命第52年。
仍是初读时的十七或十八。
刚活满52整年，引语明确如此说。
处于30多岁，且这是她唯一读书年龄。
analyses: A became Mrs.Dalloway’s age后用just broken into her fifty-second year限定，不自行改成已经活满52整年。
B Finally与became...age表明后来重读阶段，非仍在青少年。
C 进入第52年与已完成52整年不是同一个时间边界；应保留原书引语表述。
D thirties属于前次重读，不能把多个阶段合并为唯一。

vocabulary.meaning: 生命的第52年
vocabulary.context: just broken into表示刚进入这一年，与已经度过52整年有边界区别；题目沿用原句而不擅自改年龄措辞。
vocabulary.example: The quotation describes her as entering her fifty-second year.
collocations: just broken into her fifty-second year
as she became Mrs. Dalloway’s age

questions.evidenceQuote: Finally, Offill read it again as she became Mrs. Dalloway’s age, “just broken into her fifty-second year.”
